===== omerta-contracts/src/VoucherClaim.sol =====
   1: // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2: pragma solidity 0.8.26;
   3: 
   4: import {EIP712} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/EIP712.sol";
   5: import {ECDSA} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol";
   6: import {SafeERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol";
   7: import {IERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol";
   8: import {Ownable2Step, Ownable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable2Step.sol";
   9: import {Pausable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Pausable.sol";
  10: import {ReentrancyGuard} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol";
  11: 
  12: interface IGearVault {
  13:     function mint(address to, uint256 gearId, uint256 amount) external;
  14:     /// @notice Burned back toward the game so far (GearVault's re-import counter). Read on the
  15:     ///         gear path so this bridge's pre-flight bounds the same quantity the asset layer
  16:     ///         does - LIVE on-chain supply - instead of lifetime mints. See `claim`.
  17:     function redeemed(uint256 tokenId) external view returns (uint256);
  18: }
  19: 
  20: /// @title VoucherClaim - the ONLY bridge between OMERTA's game server and the chain.
  21: /// @notice The game server (off-chain authoritative) signs EIP-712 vouchers;
  22: ///         players claim them here. Security invariant, mirrored from the game
  23: ///         economy's own rule: NOTHING IS MINTED. OMR claims transfer from a
  24: ///         balance the treasury Safe pre-funded (tranches); gear claims mint
  25: ///         1155s only because the server signed that exact (player, gearId).
  26: ///         A compromised game server is bounded by the current tranche +
  27: ///         the daily cap. A compromised signer key is revoked by the Safe.
  28: contract VoucherClaim is EIP712, Ownable2Step, Pausable, ReentrancyGuard {
  29:     using SafeERC20 for IERC20;
  30: 
  31:     uint8 public constant KIND_OMR = 0;
  32:     uint8 public constant KIND_GEAR = 1;
  33: 
  34:     /// @notice Backstop on how far out a voucher's deadline may be, so a leaked
  35:     ///         (then-rotated) signer key's pre-signed vouchers can't stay claimable
  36:     ///         for months. The server signs much shorter deadlines in practice.
  37:     uint256 public constant MAX_VOUCHER_TTL = 30 days;
  38: 
  39:     bytes32 public constant VOUCHER_TYPEHASH =
  40:         keccak256("Voucher(address to,uint256 amount,uint8 kind,uint256 gearId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)");
  41: 
  42:     struct Voucher {
  43:         address to;
  44:         uint256 amount; // OMR wei for KIND_OMR; quantity (normally 1) for KIND_GEAR
  45:         uint8 kind;
  46:         uint256 gearId; // 0 for KIND_OMR
  47:         uint256 nonce; // server-unique; replay protection
  48:         uint256 deadline; // unix seconds
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     IERC20 public immutable omr;
  52:     IGearVault public immutable gear;
  53:     address public signer;
  54:     uint256 public dailyCapOMR; // max OMR claimable per UTC day, 0 = unlimited
  55:     mapping(uint256 => bool) public usedNonce;
  56:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public claimedOnDay; // day => OMR total
  57:     // Gear is bounded the same way OMR is bounded by the tranche: a per-gearId cap on LIVE
  58:     // on-chain supply the Safe sets, mirroring GearVault's own bound. FAIL-CLOSED - a gearId
  59:     // with cap 0 cannot be minted at all, so a compromised signer can't mint unknown gear.
  60:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public gearSupplyCap; // gearId => max LIVE on-chain supply (0 = mint blocked)
  61:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public gearMinted; // gearId => minted through THIS bridge so far
  62: 
  63:     event SignerSet(address indexed signer);
  64:     event DailyCapSet(uint256 cap);
  65:     event GearSupplyCapSet(uint256 indexed gearId, uint256 cap);
  66:     event Claimed(uint256 indexed nonce, address indexed to, uint8 kind, uint256 amount, uint256 gearId);
  67:     event Swept(address indexed to, uint256 amount);
  68: 
  69:     constructor(address owner_, address signer_, IERC20 omr_, IGearVault gear_, uint256 dailyCapOMR_)
  70:         EIP712("OmertaVoucherClaim", "1")
  71:         Ownable(owner_)
  72:     {
  73:         require(signer_ != address(0), "VC: zero signer");
  74:         signer = signer_;
  75:         omr = omr_;
  76:         gear = gear_;
  77:         dailyCapOMR = dailyCapOMR_;
  78:     }
  79: 
  80:     // �� admin (the Safe) ��
  81:     function setSigner(address s) external onlyOwner {
  82:         require(s != address(0), "VC: zero signer");
  83:         signer = s;
  84:         emit SignerSet(s);
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     function setDailyCap(uint256 cap) external onlyOwner {
  88:         dailyCapOMR = cap;
  89:         emit DailyCapSet(cap);
  90:     }
  91: 
  92:     /// @notice Per-gearId cap on LIVE on-chain supply - the same quantity GearVault bounds, so
  93:     ///         a re-imported (burned-back) item can be re-extracted into the slot it vacated.
  94:     ///         Must be set (> 0) before any gear of that class can be claimed. Lowering below
  95:     ///         what is already live just blocks further mints of that class.
  96:     function setGearSupplyCap(uint256 gearId, uint256 cap) external onlyOwner {
  97:         require(gearId != 0, "VC: zero gear");
  98:         gearSupplyCap[gearId] = cap;
  99:         emit GearSupplyCapSet(gearId, cap);
 100:     }
 101: 
 102:     function pause() external onlyOwner {
 103:         _pause();
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     function unpause() external onlyOwner {
 107:         _unpause();
 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     /// @notice Tranche management: the Safe can pull unspent OMR back.
 111:     function sweep(address to, uint256 amount) external onlyOwner {
 112:         omr.safeTransfer(to, amount);
 113:         emit Swept(to, amount);
 114:     }
 115: 
 116:     // �� the claim ��
 117:     function hashVoucher(Voucher calldata v) public view returns (bytes32) {
 118:         return _hashTypedDataV4(
 119:             keccak256(abi.encode(VOUCHER_TYPEHASH, v.to, v.amount, v.kind, v.gearId, v.nonce, v.deadline))
 120:         );
 121:     }
 122: 
 123:     function claim(Voucher calldata v, bytes calldata sig) external nonReentrant whenNotPaused {
 124:         require(block.timestamp <= v.deadline, "VC: expired");
 125:         require(v.deadline <= block.timestamp + MAX_VOUCHER_TTL, "VC: deadline too far");
 126:         // AUDIT hardening: explicit zero-recipient guard. The underlying ERC20/1155 would revert on
 127:         // a to==0 anyway, but a clear boundary check gives the intended custom reason (a server bug
 128:         // signing to 0x0 fails legibly) and validates external input up front (auditor checklist).
 129:         require(v.to != address(0), "VC: zero recipient");
 130:         require(!usedNonce[v.nonce], "VC: replay");
 131:         require(ECDSA.recover(hashVoucher(v), sig) == signer, "VC: bad signature");
 132:         usedNonce[v.nonce] = true;
 133: 
 134:         if (v.kind == KIND_OMR) {
 135:             uint256 day = block.timestamp / 1 days;
 136:             uint256 newTotal = claimedOnDay[day] + v.amount;
 137:             require(dailyCapOMR == 0 || newTotal <= dailyCapOMR, "VC: daily cap");
 138:             claimedOnDay[day] = newTotal;
 139:             omr.safeTransfer(v.to, v.amount); // transfers pre-funded balance; NEVER mints
 140:         } else if (v.kind == KIND_GEAR) {
 141:             require(v.gearId != 0, "VC: zero gear");
 142:             // Fail-closed per-gearId cap - bounds a compromised signer's gear blast radius the way
 143:             // the tranche bounds OMR (cap 0 => class can't mint). The bound is `minted - redeemed
 144:             // <= cap`, written as `minted <= cap + redeemed`: the EXACT expression GearVault.mint
 145:             // enforces, so the bridge's pre-flight and the asset layer measure the same quantity -
 146:             // LIVE on-chain supply. A lifetime bound here would be STRICTER than the vault's and
 147:             // would permanently kill the re-import round trip (omerta-nft-reimport-design.md 4):
 148:             // once a class had ever hit its cap, a re-imported item could never be re-extracted,
 149:             // even with every one of them burned back and zero live on-chain. Fail-closed either
 150:             // way - nothing over-mints - but the shipped feature dies, so the two must agree.
 151:             uint256 cap = gearSupplyCap[v.gearId];
 152:             uint256 minted = gearMinted[v.gearId] + v.amount;
 153:             require(cap != 0 && minted <= cap + gear.redeemed(v.gearId), "VC: gear cap");
 154:             gearMinted[v.gearId] = minted;
 155:             gear.mint(v.to, v.gearId, v.amount);
 156:         } else {
 157:             revert("VC: bad kind");
 158:         }
 159:         emit Claimed(v.nonce, v.to, v.kind, v.amount, v.gearId);
 160:     }
 161: }
===== omerta-contracts/src/DynastyNFT.sol =====
   1: // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2: pragma solidity 0.8.26;
   3: 
   4: import {ERC721} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/ERC721.sol";
   5: import {ERC2981} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/common/ERC2981.sol";
   6: import {EIP712} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/EIP712.sol";
   7: import {ECDSA} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol";
   8: import {Ownable2Step, Ownable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable2Step.sol";
   9: import {Pausable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Pausable.sol";
  10: import {ReentrancyGuard} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol";
  11: import {Strings} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Strings.sol";
  12: 
  13: /// @title DynastyNFT - OMERTA's identity NFT (omerta-dynasty-machine-design.md 4, omerta-identity-nft-design.md 5).
  14: /// @notice The player's on-chain bloodline identity: the tradeable trophy an account mints. Deliberately
  15: ///         "the plainest possible ERC-721" - it holds no value, gates nothing, and carries no 6551 code.
  16: ///
  17: ///         NO STOCK IS DELIVERED HERE, and that is a decision rather than an omission (red-team C5).
  18: ///         An earlier cut of this header named this token as the host for the ERC-6551 account
  19: ///         `StockVault` pushes tokenized stock into; the shipped rail targets the STREET DEED's
  20: ///         token-bound account instead (`src/stockdeliver.js` - own the street, and the street holds
  21: ///         your legit book). Keeping stock OFF the identity token is what preserves the wall below: a
  22: ///         token that held real assets would be a bearer instrument, and its floor would become a
  23: ///         function of its contents rather than of the bloodline it commemorates.
  24: ///
  25: ///         THE WALL (identity 1, dynasty 2.2): the game ENTITLEMENT (`account_persistent.minted`, the
  26: ///         wage/withdraw gates) stays ACCOUNT-BOUND in the backend and is NEVER read off `balanceOf`. This
  27: ///         contract therefore gates NOTHING on a balance - the trophy transfers, the entitlement does not.
  28: ///         Selling this token sells the portrait and the record; it never sells the account, the login,
  29: ///         the legends, or the extraction entitlement.
  30: ///
  31: ///         SUPPLY IS UNCAPPED (founder rule 1: a cap on the identity would cap the player count). tokenId is
  32: ///         a plain sequential counter - a dynasty is not named at mint, and the backend maps tokenId  the
  33: ///         owning account off-chain. Minting is a SERVER-SIGNED voucher self-mint (the StreetDeed / OmertaBond
  34: ///         precedent): the player pays the ETH mint fee at `OmertaFees.payMintFee()` (the fee rail is
  35: ///         unchanged, wave-priced off-chain), the backend then signs a mint voucher, and the player claims
  36: ///         their trophy (paying their own gas). There is deliberately NO owner-mint, so "the Safe was
  37: ///         compromised" and "identities were minted" stay two separate events (the OMR.minter discipline).
  38: ///         A compromised signer is bounded by the daily mint cap (rate), the nonce (no replay), the short
  39: ///         deadline (+ a MAX_VOUCHER_TTL backstop), the Safe rotating the signer - and, decisively, that the
  40: ///         token carries NO extraction entitlement, so a signer minting trophies to itself steals nothing.
  41: ///
  42: ///         tokenURI is OFF-CHAIN (the layered portrait compositor), because the portrait is LIVE game history
  43: ///         that must resolve to the OWNING ACCOUNT'S CURRENT STREET - a thing the contract cannot know - and
  44: ///         it FREEZES at the first transfer away from the minting wallet (a sold portrait is a photograph;
  45: ///         the backend owns that semantics off the standard Transfer log + the `Minted` event's minter). No
  46: ///         mutable street name, no exact field-conjunction and no wealth is engraved on-chain (the
  47: ///         walletcharacter firewall + the anti-precise-kill-EV rule); provenance traits are an OPT-IN,
  48: ///         DISPLAY-ONLY off-chain metadata attribute and touch nothing here.
  49: contract DynastyNFT is ERC721, ERC2981, EIP712, Ownable2Step, Pausable, ReentrancyGuard {
  50:     using Strings for uint256;
  51: 
  52:     /// @notice Deadline backstop (VoucherClaim.MAX_VOUCHER_TTL mirror) - a leaked-then-rotated signer key's
  53:     ///         pre-signed vouchers can't stay claimable for months. The server signs far shorter deadlines.
  54:     uint256 public constant MAX_VOUCHER_TTL = 30 days;
  55: 
  56:     bytes32 public constant MINT_VOUCHER_TYPEHASH = keccak256("MintVoucher(address to,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)");
  57: 
  58:     struct MintVoucher {
  59:         address to; // the wallet that mints (the paying player's linked wallet)
  60:         uint256 nonce; // server-unique; replay protection (also the backend's mint-request key)
  61:         uint256 deadline; // unix seconds
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     address public signer;
  65:     uint256 public dailyMintCap; // max identities mintable per UTC day, 0 = unlimited (a leaked-signer rate wall)
  66:     uint256 public nextId = 1; // sequential tokenId; uncapped collection
  67:     mapping(uint256 => bool) public usedNonce;
  68:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public mintedOnDay; // day => identities minted
  69: 
  70:     // Off-chain metadata pointer (the layered portrait + LIVE legend). Set by the Safe. tokenURI = <base><id>.
  71:     string private _baseUri;
  72: 
  73:     event SignerSet(address indexed signer);
  74:     event DailyMintCapSet(uint256 cap);
  75:     event BaseUriSet(string base);
  76:     // `minter` is the wallet the token was minted to - the backend's freeze anchor (dynamic while the current
  77:     // owner still equals `minter`, frozen once it transfers away). `nonce` ties the mint to the backend request.
  78:     event Minted(uint256 indexed nonce, address indexed minter, uint256 indexed tokenId);
  79: 
  80:     /// @dev `dailyMintCap_` is a CONSTRUCTOR argument rather than a setter-only field on purpose: this
  81:     ///      contract self-mints on the SAME signer key as VoucherClaim/OmertaBond/StreetDeed, so that key's
  82:     ///      blast radius is the SUM of the four daily caps - and with NO supply cap here, an unset wall is
  83:     ///      unbounded. A wall that lives only in a deploy checklist is one a deploy can forget; both
  84:     ///      siblings that take theirs at construction cannot be. 0 still means unlimited (the suite-wide
  85:     ///      convention), so this forces a DECISION at deploy, not a particular number.
  86:     constructor(
  87:         address owner_,
  88:         address signer_,
  89:         string memory baseUri_,
  90:         address royaltyRecipient_,
  91:         uint96 royaltyBps_,
  92:         uint256 dailyMintCap_
  93:     ) ERC721("OMERTA Dynasty", "OMERTA") EIP712("OmertaDynasty", "1") Ownable(owner_) {
  94:         require(signer_ != address(0), "DN: zero signer");
  95:         require(royaltyRecipient_ != address(0), "DN: zero royalty recipient");
  96:         signer = signer_;
  97:         _baseUri = baseUri_;
  98:         _setDefaultRoyalty(royaltyRecipient_, royaltyBps_); // EIP-2981; ERC2981 caps bps at 10000
  99:         dailyMintCap = dailyMintCap_;
 100:         emit DailyMintCapSet(dailyMintCap_);
 101:     }
 102: 
 103:     // �� admin (the Safe) ��
 104:     function setSigner(address s) external onlyOwner {
 105:         require(s != address(0), "DN: zero signer");
 106:         signer = s;
 107:         emit SignerSet(s);
 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     function setDailyMintCap(uint256 cap) external onlyOwner {
 111:         dailyMintCap = cap;
 112:         emit DailyMintCapSet(cap);
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     function setBaseUri(string calldata base_) external onlyOwner {
 116:         _baseUri = base_;
 117:         emit BaseUriSet(base_);
 118:     }
 119: 
 120:     /// @notice Rotate the EIP-2981 royalty (recipient + bps). "Royalties are ordinary and fine" (design 6);
 121:     ///         a revenue-share / floor-support framing is not - that is a COPY rule, enforced off-chain.
 122:     function setDefaultRoyalty(address recipient, uint96 bps) external onlyOwner {
 123:         require(recipient != address(0), "DN: zero royalty recipient");
 124:         _setDefaultRoyalty(recipient, bps); // ERC2981 reverts if bps > 10000
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     // Pausing stops new MINTS only; it can never trap a holder's token (there is no vault here and nothing
 128:     // is delivered here - the token simply lives in the holder's wallet).
 129:     function pause() external onlyOwner {
 130:         _pause();
 131:     }
 132: 
 133:     function unpause() external onlyOwner {
 134:         _unpause();
 135:     }
 136: 
 137:     // �� the mint (a server-signed, fee-gated-off-chain voucher self-mint) ��
 138:     function hashVoucher(MintVoucher calldata v) public view returns (bytes32) {
 139:         return _hashTypedDataV4(keccak256(abi.encode(MINT_VOUCHER_TYPEHASH, v.to, v.nonce, v.deadline)));
 140:     }
 141: 
 142:     /// @notice Mint one identity to `v.to` on a server signature. The tokenId is the next sequential id; the
 143:     ///         backend learns it from the `Minted` event (keyed by nonce  its mint request  the account).
 144:     ///         The extraction entitlement (`minted`) is set in the backend the moment the ETH fee is paid and
 145:     ///         does NOT depend on this trophy being claimed - so a player who never claims still plays fully.
 146:     function claim(MintVoucher calldata v, bytes calldata sig) external nonReentrant whenNotPaused returns (uint256) {
 147:         require(block.timestamp <= v.deadline, "DN: expired");
 148:         require(v.deadline <= block.timestamp + MAX_VOUCHER_TTL, "DN: deadline too far");
 149:         require(v.to != address(0), "DN: zero recipient");
 150:         require(!usedNonce[v.nonce], "DN: replay");
 151:         require(ECDSA.recover(hashVoucher(v), sig) == signer, "DN: bad signature");
 152:         usedNonce[v.nonce] = true;
 153: 
 154:         uint256 day = block.timestamp / 1 days;
 155:         uint256 newTotal = mintedOnDay[day] + 1;
 156:         require(dailyMintCap == 0 || newTotal <= dailyMintCap, "DN: daily cap");
 157:         mintedOnDay[day] = newTotal;
 158: 
 159:         uint256 id = nextId++;
 160:         _safeMint(v.to, id);
 161:         emit Minted(v.nonce, v.to, id);
 162:         return id;
 163:     }
 164: 
 165:     // �� metadata (off-chain, resolves to the OWNING ACCOUNT'S current street + freezes on transfer) ��
 166:     function tokenURI(uint256 id) public view override returns (string memory) {
 167:         _requireOwned(id); // reverts for a nonexistent token (ERC721NonexistentToken)
 168:         return string.concat(_baseUri, id.toString());
 169:     }
 170: 
 171:     // ERC721 + ERC2981 both declare supportsInterface - combine them.
 172:     function supportsInterface(bytes4 interfaceId) public view override(ERC721, ERC2981) returns (bool) {
 173:         return super.supportsInterface(interfaceId);
 174:     }
 175: }
===== omerta-contracts/src/GearVault.sol =====
   1: // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2: pragma solidity 0.8.26;
   3: 
   4: import {ERC1155} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC1155/ERC1155.sol";
   5: import {Ownable2Step, Ownable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable2Step.sol";
   6: import {Strings} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Strings.sol";
   7: import {Base64} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Base64.sol";
   8: 
   9: /// @title GearVault - OMERTA extractable items as ERC-1155 (gear, cars, boats).
  10: /// @notice One tokenId per item VARIANT. The tokenId is a SELF-DESCRIBING key - every scarcity trait
  11: ///         is derivable from it on-chain, with no per-token storage (this is what makes the metadata
  12: ///         "provably the token's, not a server's claim"; see `uri`):
  13: ///           * gear:  id 1..CAR_BASE-1        - a 1-based gear-class index, no rarity dimension
  14: ///           * cars:  CAR_BASE  + idx*STRIDE + rarityIndex
  15: ///           * boats: BOAT_BASE + idx*STRIDE + rarityIndex
  16: ///         These three constants MIRROR `RARITY.TOKEN` in src/rules.tail.js and the `nftTokenId`
  17: ///         helper there - they are the on-chain half of that encoding and must move in lockstep
  18: ///         (the contract/backend parity discipline used across this suite).
  19: ///
  20: ///         Minting is restricted to the VoucherClaim contract: an item enters the chain only when the
  21: ///         game server signed for it. Transfers are open - an extracted item is real property, it
  22: ///         survives the character, and (per the v3-step-7 rule) it is INERT in-game, so a liquid
  23: ///         secondary market is safe: buying one gets you a trophy, never game power.
  24: contract GearVault is ERC1155, Ownable2Step {
  25:     using Strings for uint256;
  26: 
  27:     // �� tokenId encoding (MIRRORS RARITY.TOKEN in rules.tail.js) ���������������������������������
  28:     uint256 public constant CAR_BASE = 100000;
  29:     uint256 public constant BOAT_BASE = 200000;
  30:     uint256 public constant STRIDE = 10;
  31: 
  32:     address public minter; // VoucherClaim
  33:     string private _imageBase; // e.g. "ipfs://<CID>/" - the per-tokenId plate lives at <base><id>.png
  34: 
  35:     // AUDIT (full-system-v2 G-MED-1): the per-tokenId LIFETIME supply cap is enforced HERE, at the
  36:     // asset layer, NOT only in the minter (VoucherClaim). The minter is a swappable slot; if the cap
  37:     // + minted-count lived only in the bridge, a Safe minter swap (VC-v1 -> VC-v2) would reset the
  38:     // count and let every id mint its cap AGAIN (2x+ the intended lifetime supply). GearVault
  39:     // persists across bridge upgrades, so tracking `minted` here makes "gear is fail-closed and
  40:     // bounded by a per-id supply cap" (CLAUDE.md #5) actually hold. cap 0 => class can't mint.
  41:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public cap; // tokenId => max LIVE on-chain supply (0 = mint blocked)
  42:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public minted; // tokenId => minted so far (survives a minter swap)
  43:     // NFT RE-IMPORT (Option A, omerta-nft-reimport-design.md): tokenId => burned-back-to-game so far.
  44:     // A `redeem` (burn back into the game) does NOT decrement `minted` - it increments `redeemed`, so
  45:     // the cap bounds LIVE on-chain supply (`minted - redeemed`), not lifetime mints. That vacates
  46:     // exactly one slot of headroom per burn, which a re-extraction of a re-imported item may reuse
  47:     // WITHOUT ever letting live supply exceed the cap, and without inflating true scarcity. Net item
  48:     // count across chain + game is conserved (a -1 token matched by a +1 in-game row, and vice versa).
  49:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public redeemed;
  50: 
  51:     // OPTIONAL marketplace readability: a Safe-set display name per CLASS (rarity-independent), keyed
  52:     // by the class's base tokenId (rarity digit stripped - see _classKey). Unset falls back to a
  53:     // derived "Car #<idx>" / "Boat #<idx>" / "Gear #<id>", so the vault renders fine with none set;
  54:     // set them at deploy so "GTO � Legendary" shows instead of "Car #3 � Legendary". Safe is root of
  55:     // trust, so the name is not JSON-escaped here - do not set a name containing a double-quote.
  56:     mapping(uint256 => string) public className;
  57: 
  58:     event MinterSet(address indexed minter);
  59:     event ImageBaseSet(string base);
  60:     event GearCapSet(uint256 indexed tokenId, uint256 cap);
  61:     event ClassNameSet(uint256 indexed classKey, string name);
  62:     event Redeemed(address indexed from, uint256 indexed tokenId, uint256 amount);
  63: 
  64:     constructor(address owner_, string memory imageBase_) ERC1155("") Ownable(owner_) {
  65:         _imageBase = imageBase_;
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     function setMinter(address m) external onlyOwner {
  69:         // AUDIT hardening: never let the minter be zeroed - a mis-set/zero minter silently bricks
  70:         // claims. To retire minting, pause VoucherClaim; don't strand the slot. (The lifetime cap
  71:         // now lives here, so a minter swap can never reset the per-id supply.)
  72:         require(m != address(0), "GearVault: zero minter");
  73:         minter = m;
  74:         emit MinterSet(m);
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     /// @notice The Safe sets each token's authoritative LIFETIME supply cap here. It can only be
  78:     ///         raised or held - never lowered below what's already minted - so the bound is monotone
  79:     ///         and a swapped-in minter inherits the real remaining headroom.
  80:     function setGearCap(uint256 tokenId, uint256 c) external onlyOwner {
  81:         // Never below LIVE on-chain supply (`minted - redeemed`). With re-import a token can leave the
  82:         // chain (redeem), so the floor is what's actually held on-chain, not what was ever minted -
  83:         // this lets the Safe TIGHTEN a cap as items come back to the game, while still never stranding
  84:         // a live token above the cap. (`minted >= redeemed` always, so `c + redeemed >= minted` is the
  85:         // underflow-safe form of `c >= minted - redeemed`.)
  86:         require(c + redeemed[tokenId] >= minted[tokenId], "GearVault: below live");
  87:         cap[tokenId] = c;
  88:         emit GearCapSet(tokenId, c);
  89:     }
  90: 
  91:     function setImageBase(string calldata base_) external onlyOwner {
  92:         _imageBase = base_;
  93:         emit ImageBaseSet(base_);
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     /// @notice Set the display name for a whole class (all rarities of a car/boat, or a gear class).
  97:     ///         Pass the class's BASE tokenId (rarity digit 0 for cars/boats; the gear id itself).
  98:     ///         Optional - the vault renders a derived name when unset.
  99:     function setClassName(uint256 classKey, string calldata name_) external onlyOwner {
 100:         className[classKey] = name_;
 101:         emit ClassNameSet(classKey, name_);
 102:     }
 103: 
 104:     /// @notice Batch form of setClassName for a cheap deploy of the whole catalog.
 105:     function setClassNames(uint256[] calldata classKeys, string[] calldata names) external onlyOwner {
 106:         require(classKeys.length == names.length, "GearVault: length");
 107:         for (uint256 i = 0; i < classKeys.length; i++) {
 108:             className[classKeys[i]] = names[i];
 109:             emit ClassNameSet(classKeys[i], names[i]);
 110:         }
 111:     }
 112: 
 113:     function mint(address to, uint256 tokenId, uint256 amount) external {
 114:         require(msg.sender == minter, "GearVault: not minter");
 115:         // asset-layer cap on LIVE on-chain supply - fail-closed (cap 0 blocks) and survives a minter
 116:         // swap (G-MED-1). A redeem frees exactly one slot (`redeemed`), so the bound is
 117:         // `minted - redeemed <= cap`, i.e. the number of tokens ACTUALLY on-chain never exceeds the
 118:         // cap. A re-extraction of a re-imported item reuses the slot its earlier redeem vacated,
 119:         // rather than drawing fresh lifetime supply.
 120:         uint256 m = minted[tokenId] + amount;
 121:         require(cap[tokenId] != 0 && m <= cap[tokenId] + redeemed[tokenId], "GearVault: cap");
 122:         minted[tokenId] = m;
 123:         _mint(to, tokenId, amount, "");
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// @notice Burn an extracted item (car, boat, or - since the founder-signed 7, 2026-08-21 -
 127:     ///         GEAR) back toward the game: the on-chain half of re-import
 128:     ///         (omerta-nft-reimport-design.md). The burn IS the ownership proof: only the holder can
 129:     ///         call it (`_burn` reverts otherwise), so only they can trigger a re-import to their own
 130:     ///         linked account, and no server signature is needed (unlike a mint - the event is the
 131:     ///         authority). The backend watcher re-creates the in-game row (cars/boats: on the
 132:     ///         burner's living character; gear: on their ACCOUNT) after CHAIN_CONFIRMATIONS.
 133:     ///
 134:     ///         GEAR BURNS ONE AT A TIME (`amount == 1`). Gear's in-game form is account-level SET
 135:     ///         MEMBERSHIP (account_gear), so each Redeemed event must map to exactly ONE membership
 136:     ///         change the backend's three-case rule can queue individually - a batch burn would
 137:     ///         collapse N tokens into one membership and silently destroy the rest. Cars/boats are
 138:     ///         instance rows and may batch.
 139:     ///
 140:     ///         `minted` is NOT decremented; `redeemed` is incremented, so the token vacates one
 141:     ///         live-supply slot without ever letting live supply exceed the cap (see `mint`).
 142:     function redeem(uint256 tokenId, uint256 amount) external {
 143:         require(amount != 0, "GearVault: zero");
 144:         require(tokenId != 0, "GearVault: not redeemable"); // gearId 0 is reserved (never mintable)
 145:         if (!_isCar(tokenId) && !_isBoat(tokenId)) {
 146:             require(amount == 1, "GearVault: gear one at a time");
 147:         }
 148:         _burn(msg.sender, tokenId, amount); // reverts if the caller doesn't hold `amount` - the proof
 149:         redeemed[tokenId] += amount;
 150:         emit Redeemed(msg.sender, tokenId, amount);
 151:     }
 152: 
 153:     // �� on-chain metadata ������������������������������������������������������������������������
 154:     // The type/rarity/class attributes are DERIVED from the tokenId here, so a marketplace shows the
 155:     // real, provable scarcity of the item - not a claim a server could change or fail to serve. The
 156:     // image is the one off-chain pointer (an IPFS-pinned plate), which is correct for the rich
 157:     // photographic art (see omerta-onchain-items-design.md 3/4): a 260KB JPEG can't live on-chain,
 158:     // but IPFS pins it permanently and the traits that matter for scarcity are on-chain regardless.
 159: 
 160:     function _isCar(uint256 id) internal pure returns (bool) {
 161:         return id >= CAR_BASE && id < BOAT_BASE;
 162:     }
 163: 
 164:     function _isBoat(uint256 id) internal pure returns (bool) {
 165:         return id >= BOAT_BASE;
 166:     }
 167: 
 168:     /// @dev The class's base tokenId (rarity digit stripped). Gear ids are already unique class keys.
 169:     function _classKey(uint256 id) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 170:         if (_isCar(id)) return id - ((id - CAR_BASE) % STRIDE);
 171:         if (_isBoat(id)) return id - ((id - BOAT_BASE) % STRIDE);
 172:         return id;
 173:     }
 174: 
 175:     /// @dev 0-based index of the class within its catalog (car/boat), or the gear id itself.
 176:     function _classIdx(uint256 id) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 177:         if (_isCar(id)) return (id - CAR_BASE) / STRIDE;
 178:         if (_isBoat(id)) return (id - BOAT_BASE) / STRIDE;
 179:         return id;
 180:     }
 181: 
 182:     /// @dev The rarity index (cars/boats only). Mirrors RARITY.TIERS ordering in rules.tail.js.
 183:     function _rarityIdx(uint256 id) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 184:         if (_isCar(id)) return (id - CAR_BASE) % STRIDE;
 185:         if (_isBoat(id)) return (id - BOAT_BASE) % STRIDE;
 186:         return 0;
 187:     }
 188: 
 189:     function _typeName(uint256 id) internal pure returns (string memory) {
 190:         if (_isCar(id)) return "Car";
 191:         if (_isBoat(id)) return "Boat";
 192:         return "Gear";
 193:     }
 194: 
 195:     /// @dev The four rarity names, mirroring RARITY.TIERS. A 5th tier (STRIDE leaves headroom) would
 196:     ///      add one line here - same parity discipline as the encoding constants.
 197:     function _rarityName(uint256 i) internal pure returns (string memory) {
 198:         if (i == 0) return "Common";
 199:         if (i == 1) return "Rare";
 200:         if (i == 2) return "Legendary";
 201:         if (i == 3) return "Epic";
 202:         return string.concat("Tier ", i.toString());
 203:     }
 204: 
 205:     function _displayName(uint256 id) internal view returns (string memory) {
 206:         string memory set = className[_classKey(id)];
 207:         if (bytes(set).length != 0) return set;
 208:         return string.concat(_typeName(id), " #", _classIdx(id).toString());
 209:     }
 210: 
 211:     /// @notice ERC-1155 metadata: an on-chain-assembled JSON data URI. `name`/`attributes` are
 212:     ///         derived from the tokenId (provable on-chain); `image` points to the IPFS-pinned plate.
 213:     function uri(uint256 id) public view override returns (string memory) {
 214:         string memory disp = _displayName(id);
 215:         bool rarityBearing = _isCar(id) || _isBoat(id);
 216: 
 217:         // name: "<class> � <Rarity>" for cars/boats, "<class>" for gear. Every non-ASCII glyph
 218:         // is a JSON \u escape so the whole document is ASCII bytes (unambiguous, trivially testable;
 219:         // marketplaces decode the escapes).
 220:         string memory title = rarityBearing ? string.concat(disp, " \\u00b7 ", _rarityName(_rarityIdx(id))) : disp;
 221: 
 222:         // attributes: Type + Class(number) always; Rarity for cars/boats.
 223:         string memory attrs = string.concat(
 224:             '[{"trait_type":"Type","value":"',
 225:             _typeName(id),
 226:             '"},',
 227:             '{"trait_type":"Class","value":',
 228:             _classIdx(id).toString(),
 229:             "}"
 230:         );
 231:         if (rarityBearing) {
 232:             attrs = string.concat(attrs, ',{"trait_type":"Rarity","value":"', _rarityName(_rarityIdx(id)), '"}');
 233:         }
 234:         attrs = string.concat(attrs, "]");
 235: 
 236:         string memory json = string.concat(
 237:             '{"name":"OMERT\\u00c0 ',
 238:             title,
 239:             '",',
 240:             '"description":"An extracted OMERT\\u00c0 item \\u2014 real on-chain property that survives the character. It is inert in-game (a trophy, not an advantage), which is what makes it safe to trade.",',
 241:             '"image":"',
 242:             _imageBase,
 243:             id.toString(),
 244:             '.png",',
 245:             '"attributes":',
 246:             attrs,
 247:             "}"
 248:         );
 249: 
 250:         return string.concat("data:application/json;base64,", Base64.encode(bytes(json)));
 251:     }
 252: }
===== omerta-contracts/src/StreetDeed.sol =====
   1: // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2: pragma solidity 0.8.26;
   3: 
   4: import {ERC721} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/ERC721.sol";
   5: import {EIP712} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/EIP712.sol";
   6: import {ECDSA} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol";
   7: import {Ownable2Step, Ownable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable2Step.sol";
   8: import {Pausable} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Pausable.sol";
   9: import {ReentrancyGuard} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol";
  10: import {Strings} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Strings.sol";
  11: import {Base64} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Base64.sol";
  12: 
  13: /// @title StreetDeed - the on-chain half of OMERTA's Street Deeds (omerta-street-deeds-design.md 2/3).
  14: /// @notice A named, mapped plot of the city, extracted from the game as a tradeable ERC-721 collectible.
  15: ///
  16: ///         THE ONE STRUCTURAL RULE (design 0): the DEED transfers on-chain, the game's EXTRACTION
  17: ///         ENTITLEMENT and the rent/turf CONTROL do NOT. Provenance (the legend) travels with the
  18: ///         token - it is the value - and it is served off-chain because it is LIVE game history that
  19: ///         grows. Control is earned in-game; buying this token buys a collectible with a history, never
  20: ///         game power, so a liquid secondary market is safe (the v3-step-7 rarity-NFT posture: an
  21: ///         extracted item is INERT in-game). To play the rent/turf game with a deed again, its holder
  22: ///         RE-IMPORTS it (`redeem`  the burn is the proof; the backend re-creates the in-game deed).
  23: ///
  24: ///         Minting is by a SERVER-SIGNED voucher only - there is deliberately no owner-mint, so "the
  25: ///         Safe was compromised" and "deeds were minted" stay two separate events (the OMR.minter
  26: ///         discipline). A compromised signer is bounded by: the daily mint cap (rate), the nonce
  27: ///         (no replay), the short deadline (+ a MAX_VOUCHER_TTL backstop), the Safe rotating the
  28: ///         signer - and, decisively, that a deed carries NO extraction value (the `minted` flag does
  29: ///         not travel), so a signer that mints trophies to itself steals nothing a player can cash out.
  30: ///
  31: ///         tokenId = uint256(keccak256(bytes(name))). The server signs the canonical street NAME and
  32: ///         the contract DERIVES the tokenId, so the nametokenId map is a bijection enforced on-chain:
  33: ///         a voucher can never claim one tokenId for a different name, and a name can be minted at most
  34: ///         once (ERC-721 `_safeMint` reverts on an existing token). After a `redeem` burns it the token
  35: ///         no longer exists, so a fresh voucher (new nonce) can re-extract the SAME street - the id is
  36: ///         stable across round-trips because the name never changes.
  37: contract StreetDeed is ERC721, EIP712, Ownable2Step, Pausable, ReentrancyGuard {
  38:     using Strings for uint256;
  39: 
  40:     /// @notice Deadline backstop, mirroring VoucherClaim.MAX_VOUCHER_TTL - a leaked-then-rotated
  41:     ///         signer key's pre-signed vouchers can't stay claimable for months. The server signs
  42:     ///         much shorter deadlines in practice.
  43:     uint256 public constant MAX_VOUCHER_TTL = 30 days;
  44: 
  45:     bytes32 public constant DEED_VOUCHER_TYPEHASH =
  46:         keccak256("DeedVoucher(address to,string name,string district,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)");
  47: 
  48:     struct DeedVoucher {
  49:         address to;
  50:         string name; // the canonical street name; tokenId = uint256(keccak256(bytes(name)))
  51:         string district; // the mapped district (display string) - on-chain identity, immutable
  52:         uint256 nonce; // server-unique; replay protection
  53:         uint256 deadline; // unix seconds
  54:     }
  55: 
  56:     address public signer;
  57:     uint256 public dailyMintCap; // max deeds mintable per UTC day, 0 = unlimited (a leaked-signer rate wall)
  58:     mapping(uint256 => bool) public usedNonce;
  59:     mapping(uint256 => uint256) public mintedOnDay; // day => deeds minted
  60: 
  61:     // �� on-chain identity (immutable per token; survives the game server being down) ��
  62:     mapping(uint256 => string) public deedName;
  63:     /// @notice THE LISTING LOCK (design 5, drain-before-sale) - every deed is NON-TRANSFERABLE by
  64:     ///         default: minted locked, and RE-LOCKED on every transfer, so each new owner starts
  65:     ///         locked too. Selling is a deliberate two-step - the OWNER (never an approved operator:
  66:     ///         a marketplace approval must not be able to unlock, that is the drain vector) calls
  67:     ///         setTransferLock(id, false), which emits a public event a buyer can anchor on: check
  68:     ///         the deed's ERC-6551 vault CONTENTS after the unlock block - anything drained between
  69:     ///         unlock and sale is visible on-chain in that window. Not an escrow and not airtight
  70:     ///         (an unlocked deed can still be drained pre-sale - the event makes it VISIBLE, which
  71:     ///         is the design's stated preference over a custody scheme); redeem() is NEVER blocked
  72:     ///         by the lock - a lock that trapped the holder's own burn-back would violate the
  73:     ///         never-trap rule the pause already honors.
  74:     mapping(uint256 => bool) public transferLocked;
  75:     mapping(uint256 => string) public deedDistrict;
  76: 
  77:     // Off-chain pointers for the rich, LIVE parts (the block plate + the legend page). Set by the Safe.
  78:     // The identity (name/district) is on-chain; only the image and the "see its full history" link are
  79:     // off-chain, which is correct: the legend GROWS with play and cannot be immutable.
  80:     string private _imageBase; // e.g. "https://www.omerta.fun/v1/deeds/plate/"  <base><id>.svg
  81:     string private _externalBase; // e.g. "https://www.omerta.fun/deed/"             <base><id>
  82: 
  83:     event SignerSet(address indexed signer);
  84:     event DailyMintCapSet(uint256 cap);
  85:     event ImageBaseSet(string base);
  86:     event ExternalBaseSet(string base);
  87:     event TransferLockSet(uint256 indexed tokenId, bool locked, address indexed by);
  88:     event Extracted(uint256 indexed nonce, address indexed to, uint256 indexed tokenId, string name, string district);
  89:     event Redeemed(address indexed from, uint256 indexed tokenId);
  90: 
  91:     /// @dev `dailyMintCap_` is a CONSTRUCTOR argument rather than a setter-only field on purpose: this
  92:     ///      contract self-mints on the SAME signer key as VoucherClaim/OmertaBond/DynastyNFT, so that key's
  93:     ///      blast radius is the SUM of the four daily caps - and a wall that lives only in a deploy
  94:     ///      checklist is one a deploy can forget. Both siblings that take theirs at construction cannot be
  95:     ///      forgotten; these two could, and were. 0 still means unlimited (the suite-wide convention), so
  96:     ///      this forces a DECISION at deploy, not a particular number.
  97:     constructor(
  98:         address owner_,
  99:         address signer_,
 100:         string memory imageBase_,
 101:         string memory externalBase_,
 102:         uint256 dailyMintCap_
 103:     ) ERC721("OMERTA Street Deed", "STREET") EIP712("OmertaStreetDeed", "1") Ownable(owner_) {
 104:         require(signer_ != address(0), "SD: zero signer");
 105:         signer = signer_;
 106:         _imageBase = imageBase_;
 107:         _externalBase = externalBase_;
 108:         dailyMintCap = dailyMintCap_;
 109:         emit DailyMintCapSet(dailyMintCap_);
 110:     }
 111: 
 112:     // �� admin (the Safe) ��
 113:     function setSigner(address s) external onlyOwner {
 114:         require(s != address(0), "SD: zero signer");
 115:         signer = s;
 116:         emit SignerSet(s);
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     function setDailyMintCap(uint256 cap) external onlyOwner {
 120:         dailyMintCap = cap;
 121:         emit DailyMintCapSet(cap);
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     function setImageBase(string calldata base_) external onlyOwner {
 125:         _imageBase = base_;
 126:         emit ImageBaseSet(base_);
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     function setExternalBase(string calldata base_) external onlyOwner {
 130:         _externalBase = base_;
 131:         emit ExternalBaseSet(base_);
 132:     }
 133: 
 134:     // Pausing stops new EXTRACTIONS (claims) only; `redeem` is never pausable so a holder can always
 135:     // bring their property back into the game - a pause that traps property is a rug the design forbids.
 136:     function pause() external onlyOwner {
 137:         _pause();
 138:     }
 139: 
 140:     function unpause() external onlyOwner {
 141:         _unpause();
 142:     }
 143: 
 144:     // �� the extraction (claim) ��
 145:     function tokenIdFor(string memory name) public pure returns (uint256) {
 146:         return uint256(keccak256(bytes(name)));
 147:     }
 148: 
 149:     function hashVoucher(DeedVoucher calldata v) public view returns (bytes32) {
 150:         return _hashTypedDataV4(
 151:             keccak256(
 152:                 abi.encode(
 153:                     DEED_VOUCHER_TYPEHASH,
 154:                     v.to,
 155:                     keccak256(bytes(v.name)),
 156:                     keccak256(bytes(v.district)),
 157:                     v.nonce,
 158:                     v.deadline
 159:                 )
 160:             )
 161:         );
 162:     }
 163: 
 164:     /// @notice Mint (extract) the deed named `v.name` to `v.to`, on a server signature. tokenId is
 165:     ///         derived from the name, so a name is minted at most once (a duplicate reverts in
 166:     ///         `_safeMint`). The extraction entitlement (`minted`) and the rent/turf control stay in
 167:     ///         the game - this only issues the collectible.
 168:     function claim(DeedVoucher calldata v, bytes calldata sig) external nonReentrant whenNotPaused {
 169:         require(block.timestamp <= v.deadline, "SD: expired");
 170:         require(v.deadline <= block.timestamp + MAX_VOUCHER_TTL, "SD: deadline too far");
 171:         require(v.to != address(0), "SD: zero recipient");
 172:         require(bytes(v.name).length != 0, "SD: empty name");
 173:         require(!usedNonce[v.nonce], "SD: replay");
 174:         require(ECDSA.recover(hashVoucher(v), sig) == signer, "SD: bad signature");
 175:         usedNonce[v.nonce] = true;
 176: 
 177:         uint256 day = block.timestamp / 1 days;
 178:         uint256 newTotal = mintedOnDay[day] + 1;
 179:         require(dailyMintCap == 0 || newTotal <= dailyMintCap, "SD: daily cap");
 180:         mintedOnDay[day] = newTotal;
 181: 
 182:         uint256 id = tokenIdFor(v.name);
 183:         deedName[id] = v.name;
 184:         deedDistrict[id] = v.district;
 185:         _safeMint(v.to, id); // reverts if the name (tokenId) already exists - one deed per name, ever
 186: 
 187:         emit Extracted(v.nonce, v.to, id, v.name, v.district);
 188:     }
 189: 
 190:     /// @notice Burn the deed back toward the game - the on-chain half of re-import. The burn IS the
 191:     ///         ownership proof (only the holder can call it), so no server signature is needed (the
 192:     ///         event is the authority, exactly like GearVault.redeem). The backend watcher re-creates
 193:     ///         the in-game deed on whoever burned it after CHAIN_CONFIRMATIONS. After the burn the token
 194:     ///         no longer exists, so the same street can be re-extracted later with a fresh voucher.
 195:     /// @notice Lock or unlock a deed for transfer. Owner-only - deliberately NOT approved
 196:     ///         operators (see transferLocked). Unlocking is the public "listing" act.
 197:     function setTransferLock(uint256 tokenId, bool locked) external {
 198:         require(ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender, "SD: not owner");
 199:         transferLocked[tokenId] = locked;
 200:         emit TransferLockSet(tokenId, locked, msg.sender);
 201:     }
 202: 
 203:     function redeem(uint256 tokenId) external {
 204:         require(ownerOf(tokenId) == msg.sender, "SD: not owner"); // reverts if nonexistent - clean
 205:         _burn(tokenId);
 206:         // Keep the name/district for a possible re-extraction's metadata; they are immutable and
 207:         // re-derive identically from the same name anyway, so leaving them is harmless and cheaper.
 208:         emit Redeemed(msg.sender, tokenId);
 209:     }
 210: 
 211:     /// @dev The lock's enforcement point. Mint (from == 0) and burn (to == 0) pass - a claim must
 212:     ///      land and redeem() must never be blocked - but an owner-to-owner transfer requires the
 213:     ///      current owner to have unlocked first, and the deed RE-LOCKS the moment it arrives so
 214:     ///      the default-ON invariant holds for every owner, not just the first.
 215:     function _update(address to, uint256 tokenId, address auth) internal override returns (address) {
 216:         address from = _ownerOf(tokenId);
 217:         if (from != address(0) && to != address(0)) {
 218:             require(!transferLocked[tokenId], "SD: locked - unlock before transfer");
 219:         }
 220:         address prev = super._update(to, tokenId, auth);
 221:         if (to == address(0)) delete transferLocked[tokenId]; // burn: clear the slot
 222:         else transferLocked[tokenId] = true; // mint OR arrival: locked
 223:         return prev;
 224:     }
 225: 
 226:     // �� on-chain metadata ������������������������������������������������������������������������
 227:     // Identity (name + district) is assembled ON-CHAIN, so a marketplace shows the real street even if
 228:     // the game server is down. The image (the block plate) and external_url (the legend page) are the
 229:     // off-chain pointers, which is correct: the plate and the LIVE legend grow with play. Marketing
 230:     // guardrails (design 6) bind this string: property with a history, never "scarce/appreciating land".
 231:     function tokenURI(uint256 id) public view override returns (string memory) {
 232:         _requireOwned(id); // reverts for a nonexistent/burned token (ERC721NonexistentToken)
 233:         string memory nm = _json(deedName[id]);
 234:         string memory dt = _json(deedDistrict[id]);
 235:         string memory json = string.concat(
 236:             '{"name":"',
 237:             nm,
 238:             '",',
 239:             '"description":"A Street Deed \\u2014 a named, mapped plot in the city of OMERT\\u00c0. Its worth is the story on it: everything that ever happened here. Property with a history.",',
 240:             '"image":"',
 241:             _imageBase,
 242:             id.toString(),
 243:             '.svg",',
 244:             '"external_url":"',
 245:             _externalBase,
 246:             id.toString(),
 247:             '",',
 248:             '"attributes":[',
 249:             '{"trait_type":"Type","value":"Street Deed"},',
 250:             '{"trait_type":"District","value":"',
 251:             dt,
 252:             '"}',
 253:             "]}"
 254:         );
 255:         return string.concat("data:application/json;base64,", Base64.encode(bytes(json)));
 256:     }
 257: 
 258:     // Minimal JSON string sanitizer: a deed name is player-chosen, and the backend already strips
 259:     // < > " at claim (cleanText), but a marketplace parses this document, so we escape the two bytes
 260:     // that could break the JSON regardless - a backslash and a double-quote. Control bytes are not
 261:     // reachable (the name filter drops them), so this is belt-and-braces on the two structural chars.
 262:     function _json(string memory s) internal pure returns (string memory) {
 263:         bytes memory b = bytes(s);
 264:         bytes memory out = new bytes(b.length * 2);
 265:         uint256 n = 0;
 266:         for (uint256 i = 0; i < b.length; i++) {
 267:             bytes1 c = b[i];
 268:             if (c == '"' || c == "\\") {
 269:                 out[n++] = "\\";
 270:                 out[n++] = c;
 271:             } else {
 272:                 out[n++] = c;
 273:             }
 274:         }
 275:         bytes memory trimmed = new bytes(n);
 276:         for (uint256 i = 0; i < n; i++) {
 277:             trimmed[i] = out[i];
 278:         }
 279:         return string(trimmed);
 280:     }
 281: }

 130:     /// @notice Mint OMR. Callable ONLY by `minter` - on mainnet the OmertaBond contract, whose three
 131:     ///         walls (daily cap, discount ceiling, mint-rate ceiling) are what bound issuance. There
 132:     ///         is deliberately no owner mint: the Safe chooses WHO may mint and can revoke it, but
 133:     ///         cannot itself print, so "the Safe was compromised" and "supply was inflated" stay two
 134:     ///         separate events rather than one.
 135:     function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {
 136:         if (msg.sender != minter || minter == address(0)) revert NotMinter();

 144:     /// @notice Arm/tune the DEX sell tax (<= 10% total) and how it splits. Recipients must be set
 145:     ///         first. `devBps + rwaBps + communityBps <= bps`; LP takes the remainder.
 146:     function setSellTax(uint256 bps, uint256 devBps, uint256 rwaBps, uint256 communityBps) external onlyOwner {
 147:         if (bps > MAX_SELL_TAX_BPS) revert BadBps();

 188:     function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {
 189:         // a SELL (or a non-exempt LP add): carve the tax to the two revenue wallets in-transfer
 190:         if (sellTaxBps > 0 && ammPairs[to] && from != address(0) && !taxExempt[from]) {
 191:             uint256 tax = (value * sellTaxBps) / 10000;
 192:             if (tax > 0) {
 193:                 // The remainder rule sits on the LP slice, so dev + rwa + community + lp == tax
 194:                 // EXACTLY however the bps divide - the same discipline the backend's sell-tax ingest
 195:                 // uses, for the same reason: three of four shares round down, and a "natural" last
 196:                 // slice would leave a wei belonging to nobody stranded in the seller's balance.
 197:                 uint256 dev = (tax * taxDevBps) / sellTaxBps;
 198:                 uint256 rwa = (tax * taxRwaBps) / sellTaxBps;
 199:                 uint256 community = (tax * taxCommunityBps) / sellTaxBps;

  49:     function setApy(uint256 bps) external onlyOwner {
  50:         require(bps <= MAX_APY_BPS, "Staking: apy too high");
  51:         // Settle the elapsed interval at the OLD rate before changing it. Without this checkpoint,
  52:         // raising APY reprices every user's entire unclaimed history at the new rate (and lowering it
  53:         // confiscates already-earned rewards). The global index avoids iterating over stakers.
  54:         _updateRewardIndex();
  55:         apyBps = bps;
  56:         emit ApySet(bps);
  57:     }
  58: 
  59:     /// @notice The Safe funds rewards explicitly - never confused with principal.
  60:     function fundRewards(uint256 amount) external {
  61:         omr.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
  62:         rewardPool += amount;
  63:         emit PoolFunded(amount);
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     function _updateRewardIndex() internal {
  67:         uint256 elapsed = block.timestamp - lastRewardUpdate;
  68:         if (elapsed > 0) {
  69:             rewardIndex += (apyBps * elapsed * 1e18) / (10_000 * YEAR);
  70:             lastRewardUpdate = uint64(block.timestamp);
  71:         }
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     function _accrue(address user) internal {
  75:         _updateRewardIndex();
  76:         Position storage p = positions[user];
  77:         if (p.staked > 0) {
  78:             p.accrued += (p.staked * (rewardIndex - rewardIndexPaid[user])) / 1e18;
  79:         }
  80:         rewardIndexPaid[user] = rewardIndex;
  81:         p.lastAccrued = uint64(block.timestamp);
  82:     }
  83: 
  84:     function stake(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {
  85:         require(amount > 0, "Staking: zero");
  86:         _accrue(msg.sender);
  87:         omr.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
  88:         positions[msg.sender].staked += amount;
  89:         totalStaked += amount;
  90:         emit Staked(msg.sender, amount);
  91:     }
  92: 
  93:     function unstake(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {
  94:         _accrue(msg.sender);
  95:         Position storage p = positions[msg.sender];
  96:         require(amount > 0 && amount <= p.staked, "Staking: bad amount");
  97:         p.staked -= amount;
  98:         totalStaked -= amount;

 100:         emit Unstaked(msg.sender, amount);

 103:     function claimRewards() external nonReentrant {
 104:         _accrue(msg.sender);
 105:         Position storage p = positions[msg.sender];
 106:         uint256 amount = p.accrued;
 107:         require(amount > 0, "Staking: nothing accrued");
 108:         require(amount <= rewardPool, "Staking: pool dry");
 109:         p.accrued = 0;
 110:         rewardPool -= amount;
 111:         omr.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount);
 112:         emit RewardsClaimed(msg.sender, amount);
 113:     }

 115:     function pendingRewards(address user) external view returns (uint256) {
 116:         Position memory p = positions[user];
 117:         uint256 liveIndex = rewardIndex;

 404:     /// @notice Push accrued fees to the four wallets. Permissionless - it cannot send anywhere but

 406:     ///         Deliberately NOT done inside the swap: a recipient that reverts on receipt would then

 408:     function sweep(Currency currency) external {
 409:         Owed memory o = owed[currency];
 410:         if (o.dev == 0 && o.rwa == 0 && o.community == 0 && o.lp == 0) revert NothingToSweep();

 412:         // UNREACHABLE defence in depth, which is worth saying rather than leaving a reader to wonder.

Checks covered reentrancy/callbacks, authorization/replay, rounding/conservation, oracle history/freshness/liquidity, configuration/lifecycle recovery, and privilege/economic boundaries.
    26: 
    27: ## Findings and dispositions
    28: 
    29: ### RT-M02 / historical M-02 - medium, conditional unsupported oracle price
    30: 
    31: Affected path: `OmertaHook`  `OmrV4TwapOracle`, when an initialized pool has zero active liquidity. Initialization does not require liquidity; a zero-delta swap can change its tick; the hook accrues that tick; the oracle later publishes the resulting interval as fresh.
    32: 
    33: The executed `ComprehensiveMarketAudit.test_risk_emptyLiquidityProducesZeroCostFreshTwap` moves square-root price from Q96 to 2xQ96 without paying either asset and observes approximately 4x the original OMR/ETH quote. This establishes unsupported-price publication. It does **not** prove theft from a deployed bond: an economic-loss path additionally needs a consumer trusting that feed, absent liquidity and issuance/authorization conditions that permit use of the quote.
    34: 
    35: Disposition: **open, conditional; no clearance for consumers of this oracle under absent liquidity**. This historical finding was preserved rather than rewritten as a newly discovered exploit. The current market's observation/state path rejects zero-liquidity epochs; this does not clear other consumers. Remediation for any activation of the affected feed must validate liquidity across the entire observation interval, or use an independently depth-qualified feed and retest the consumer. A spot-only liquidity check would not establish that interval property.
    36: 
    37: ### RT-P01 - acquisition funding/activation blocker
    38: 
    39: `AcquisitionVault`/`AcquisitionVaultCore` accept custody/accounting ingress but lack a complete corresponding asset release path. The authority's unpause fails closed and intent execution/reconciliation contain staged surfaces. Slither's two locked-ether diagnostics are accurate implementation/phase limitations, not false positives.
    40: 
    41: Disposition: **do not fund or activate these rails as a functioning acquisition system**. Existing local guards do not supply a withdrawal facility. No privileged or public theft was demonstrated. Completing execution/outflow changes reopens review.
    42: 
    43: ### Configuration and operational residuals
    44: 
    45: - Immutable genesis-splitter recipients must accept ETH. One permanently rejecting recipient blocks the atomic distribution. No attacker-controlled redirection was established. ETH held before pool initialization is permissionlessly recoverable to the fixed treasury; pre-migration funding order must match this intended behavior.
    46: - Player-sale settlement is permissionless and per-wallet; all participants must settle before proceeds release. Eligibility cardinality, keeper enumeration and deadline capacity need launch-specific rehearsal. Cancellation preserves the tested refund path; unavoidable/profitable settlement DoS was not demonstrated.
    47: - Codehash pinning verifies runtime identity, not proxy implementation/storage immutability or semantic correctness. Actual manager, Permit2, auction, hook, Safe and asset selections require verification.
    48: - Standard-token and selected ERC4626 valuation/withdrawal behavior are external assumptions. Fee-on-transfer, rebasing, callbacks and upgrades need configuration-specific validation.
    49: - Turf adjudication, signer decisions, health feeds and governance remain explicit trusted authorities. No privilege-escalation path was confirmed; correctness of off-chain truth was outside scope.
    50: - Cancun transient-storage support is a deployment prerequisite for the vendored guard.
    51: 
    52: These conditions are not silently accepted on the owner's behalf and prevent a universal deployment-ready conclusion.
    53: 
    54: ## Closed hypotheses
    55: 
    56: The [market review](market-review.md) retains the actual dependency trace showing position-manager mutation requires current NFT-owner/approval authority, while transfer into the commitment vault clears token approval. Depositor/operator permissions cannot remove locked position liquidity through that manager. Invalid/stale observation anchors cannot backfill rewards; maturity withdrawal does not depend on oracle state.
    57: 
    58: The extreme genesis inversion input is excluded by the documented auction floor and monotone clearing price. Matching-reserve adequacy remains an explicit configuration requirement with integer/finite-range margin; no inadequate supported-configuration witness was established. The report retains the reserve calculation rather than claiming unspecified final parameters are safe.
    59: 
    60: Mythril's three high arithmetic diagnostics target optimized comparisons in `cap(uint8)`. The new [exhaustive test](../../test/audit/PlayerSaleCapDomain.t.sol) checks every uint8 input against the five published caps or the exact eligibility error and passes. Five environment/deadline diagnostics are intentional phase predicates. [Symbolic triage](mythril-triage.json) preserves each warning. Runtime-only symbolic execution starts with unconstrained storage and was bounded to 60 seconds, two transactions and depth 32; it is not a whole-contract proof.

    79: 
    80: ## Negative attack traces and invariants
    81: 
    82: ### Bank and staking
    83: 
    84: [Feynman: Alchemist/CollateralEscrow] Each user owns a private container of external vault shares. Deposits buy shares; withdrawals sell enough shares to pay the requested asset amount. Borrowing records debt, then creates DNR. Harvest sells only value above the recorded principal and moves net proceeds into redemption reserves.
    85: 
    86: [Inversion: bank] Three attacks were traced: donate before another user's deposit to dilute their shares; borrow just past prospective reserve headroom; harvest a position at its LTV with an exit-fee vault. The caller's mandatory nonzero `minSharesOut` and actual share delta block the first from being silently accepted; the second mint rolls back at its post-mint `bufferHealthy` check; fee-aware valuation and the harvest post-state debt ceiling roll back the third before debt/backing divergence persists.
    87: 
    88: Concrete rounding check: yield=4 underlying units, fee=20%, debt at least 4*scale. net=4; naive fee=1; the clamp reduces fee to 0 so withdrawal=4, not 5. Debt reduction is at most moved net assets*scale. Repayment of residual debt d<scale pulls ceil(d/scale)=1 asset unit and clears only d; redemption floors to debtAmount/scale and rejects output=0. No positive rounding roundtrip was found.
    89: 
    90: [Feynman: OMRStaking] User deposits add only principal; rewards accrue with time and are paid only from an independently funded pool. An APY change closes the prior interval before installing the new rate.
    91: 
    92: [Inversion: staking] Claim with rewardPool=0; stake and claim at the same timestamp; enter after a long period of no stake. Pool-dry claims revert without removing principal. Stake first records the current reward index, so entry does not inherit past rewards. Unstake never tests rewardPool. Small flooring can reduce accrued dust; no path makes another user's principal available for reward payout with the intended exact-transfer OMR configuration.
    93: 
    94: ### Authorization, callbacks and accounting
    95: 
    96: [Feynman: vouchers] A signed voucher chooses its recipient and amount. Anyone can submit it, but the value goes to the signed recipient and a nonce is consumed before token/NFT receiver code runs.
    97: 
    98: [Inversion: vouchers] Reuse a nonce; alter recipient/amount/gear ID; recursively claim during an ERC721/1155 callback. Domain/field hashing and nonce checks block the first two; claim guards block the third. Gear receiver burn during mint is allowed, but both minted and redeemed remain accounted, so `minted-redeemed<=cap` remains the cap model. StreetDeed holder may redeem during receipt; downstream event consumers must handle actual receipt/log order, and this source-only pass does not prove backend indexing semantics.
    99: 
   100: [Feynman: acquisition] Money arriving through the committed ingress becomes available, except money needed to repair a previous balance deficit. Forced money remains unattributed until the Safe explicitly reclassifies it.
   101: 
   102: [Inversion: acquisition] Force ETH and sync twice; rotate ingress to reset global lifetime credit; deposit during deficit and count the repair twice. `syncBalance` moves only current surplus, cumulative global deposits survive ingress generation changes, and `credit=msg.value-min(msg.value,preDeficit)` distinguishes repair from availability. Accounting identifiers bind chain/core/module/generation/sequence. Factory advances its phase before constructor/finalizer calls, preventing nested deployment progression. Remaining reservation/reconciliation balances cannot currently be changed by an executable outflow path.
   103: 
   104: [Socratic: AcquisitionAuthority pending getters] The manually numbered slots depend on the exact compiler/inheritance storage layout, not merely the struct definition. The coordinating reviewer executed `forge inspect AcquisitionAuthority storage-layout --json` and confirmed nomination slot 9, ingress proposal slot 18 and ingress mapping slot 29. The retained compiler/settings remain essential to this equivalence.
   105: 
   106: [Feynman: settlement] Crediting reserves an amount for one executor; withdrawing removes that reservation before paying the executor. Migration may spend only unreserved ETH.
   107: 
   108: [Inversion: settlement] Withdraw recursively; return the payment as a contribution during callback; migrate funds after credits consumed proposal headroom. The withdrawal guard/zeroed credit block double withdrawal; a callback contribution adds genuine assets without recreating the executor liability; migration rechecks its amount against current unreserved balance. Cost multiplication/addition saturate at the configured settlement cap instead of wrapping. The caller supplied `measuredSettlementGas` is trusted only because the entry point is restricted to gameplayVault; this pass did not prove its measurement implementation.
   109: 
   110: ### Liquidity, prices and RWA
   111: 
   112: [Feynman: ProtocolLiquidityVault] The vault holds one authenticated full-range liquidity NFT. Automation adds liquidity from inventory under action/window budgets; earned fees are collected and paid to fixed destinations. Emergency recovery moves the NFT and free inventory to the original configured Safe.
   113: 
   114: [Inversion: liquidity] Present an NFT from another pool or subscribed position; steal a standing Permit2 allowance; recursively invoke the swap callback. Foundation identity/range/owner/liquidity/subscriber checks reject the first. Exact allowances are zeroed after modification, and failed transactions roll back. Buyback callback requires the manager plus its armed one-shot flag, clears that flag before swapping, and checks actual ETH/OMR deltas after settlement. LP adds isolate collected fees from input inventory; native manager dust is explicitly included in accounting rather than falsely counted as negative spend.
   115: 
   116: [Feynman: oracles] The pair/hook records time spent at each price. A completed average is converted into the interface's OMR wei per ETH; consumers enforce recency and nonzero output.
   117: 
   118: [Inversion: oracles] Manipulate only within one timestamp; use a reversed/noncanonical V2 pair; update after an excessive window. Same-timestamp manipulation does not retroactively add elapsed price time; constructor pair/token-order checks reject substitution; windows beyond four periods invalidate and rebaseline. V4 negative cumulative division rounds down deliberately. A long-duration price manipulation remains an economic assumption; no live pool depth or manipulation-cost claim was verified here. Constructor-supplied PERIOD values near the uint32 limit can make `PERIOD*4` overflow; these represent multi-decade windows and are configuration misuse, not a live unprivileged exploit claim.
   119: 
   120: [Feynman: RWA] The catalog binds token versions to symbols/provider identities. Published ballots keep the original version/generation. Buying pays the approved adapter, but only succeeds if the StockVault receives at least the oracle/caller output floor.
   121: 
   122: [Inversion: RWA] Keeper sets tiny minUnits; deactivate/reactivate a ballot asset under the same key; forged delivery alters destination. Buyer uses max(oracle floor, keeper floor) and an actual destination-balance delta. Registry generation mismatch keeps the old ballot inactive even after same-key reactivation; overlay clearance independently binds activation generation. StockVault allocation signatures bind delivery/token/to/units, with replay consumed before transfer. With allocationSigner=0, delivery is explicitly keeper-trusted and cap-limited rather than two-authority delivery; deployment must identify the intended mode.
   123: 
   124: ## Findings, leads and unresolved verification
   125: 
   126: Confirmed findings: **none added by this reviewer**. No `[POC-PASS]` tag is claimed. There is no locally identified unit/property exploit hypothesis needing an unattempted mandatory harm PoC.
   127: 
   128: **Retained historical oracle residual (M02):** `OmertaHook`/`OmrV4TwapOracle` root implementation observations do not gate the accumulated tick on active liquidity. The coordinating test `test/audit/ComprehensiveMarketAudit.t.sol::test_risk_emptyLiquidityProducesZeroCostFreshTwap` initializes a zero-liquidity pool, executes a public swap with zero ETH/OMR balance delta that moves sqrtPrice from Q96 to 2*Q96, advances 600 seconds and reads approximately 4e18 OMR/ETH with a fresh timestamp. This is a conditional mechanism witness, not a new confirmed loss: exploitation requires a value-consuming rail to be armed while usable liquidity is absent. The separately configured liquidity health guard must fail closed, and deployment/consumer wiring remains mandatory verification. The historical M02 status must not be erased or presented as a new fix in this review. Mechanical execution of this witness is recorded in the coordinating package, not claimed independently here.
   129: 
   130: One integration lead was handed to the coordinating reviewer: `GenesisProceedsSplitter.recoverFailedLaunch()` is permissionless and checks only whether the canonical pool is initialized. If an actual deployment intentionally parks launch ETH there across transactions before initialization, any caller can route it early to treasury. Fixed destinations mean the caller cannot steal it. The current strategy integration appears intended to send residual atomically with migration, but the exact strategy and deployed funding order were not verified by this reviewer. Status: **LEAD; external/deployment prerequisite unverified**, not confirmed launch sabotage. PoC class: integration; local attempt: no; blocker: actual strategy/funding order outside this root-file scope (`EXTERNAL_DEP_NO_FORK` / deployment ordering). Resolve against the auction/strategy review before making a launch-readiness claim.
   131: 
   132: Other limitations are trust/configuration facts rather than vulnerability findings:
   133: 
   134: - AcquisitionCore, AcquisitionVault and constellation helpers are source-stage ingress/accounting rails with no withdrawal/purchase execution entry point. `AcquisitionAuthority.unpause` always reverts `LocalReadinessFailed(11)`. Do not fund/activate these as a completed purchase rail without the separate release work.
   135: - `codehash` pins bytecode identity, not an underlying proxy implementation's governance. Trusted external asset/vault/oracle/router/migration semantics require separate deployment evidence.
   136: - Several caps intentionally use zero=unlimited. Source checks do not prove live caps, signer separation, supported-chain identity, configured minter/burner, correct OMR tax exemptions, health guard installation or treasury recipients.
   137: - Direct-push fixed-recipient routes can revert if recipients reject ETH; documented Safe-selected recipients and recovery/configuration abilities are part of that trust model. No unprivileged way to replace a recipient was found.
   138: - Backend signer issuance, entitlement accounting, NFT reimport/event processing, database concurrency and actual gameplayVault gas measurement were not reviewed here.
   139: - The coordinating evidence package must supply executed unit/fuzz/invariant outputs, raw static-analysis findings and triage. This subreport supplies source review and hypotheses, not an independently clean static-analysis result.

   188:     function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {
   189:         // a SELL (or a non-exempt LP add): carve the tax to the two revenue wallets in-transfer
   190:         if (sellTaxBps > 0 && ammPairs[to] && from != address(0) && !taxExempt[from]) {
   191:             uint256 tax = (value * sellTaxBps) / 10000;
   192:             if (tax > 0) {
   193:                 // The remainder rule sits on the LP slice, so dev + rwa + community + lp == tax
   194:                 // EXACTLY however the bps divide - the same discipline the backend's sell-tax ingest
   195:                 // uses, for the same reason: three of four shares round down, and a "natural" last
   196:                 // slice would leave a wei belonging to nobody stranded in the seller's balance.
   197:                 uint256 dev = (tax * taxDevBps) / sellTaxBps;
   198:                 uint256 rwa = (tax * taxRwaBps) / sellTaxBps;
   199:                 uint256 community = (tax * taxCommunityBps) / sellTaxBps;
   200:                 uint256 lp = tax - dev - rwa - community;
   201:                 if (dev > 0) super._update(from, taxDevRecipient, dev);
   202:                 if (rwa > 0) super._update(from, taxRwaRecipient, rwa);
   203:                 if (community > 0) super._update(from, taxCommunityRecipient, community);
   204:                 if (lp > 0) super._update(from, taxLpRecipient, lp);
   205:                 emit SellTaxTaken(from, to, tax);
   206:                 value -= tax;
   207:             }
   208:         }
   209:         super._update(from, to, value);
   210:     }
   211: }

   110:         factory = factory_;
   111:         pair = pair_;
   112:         omr = omr_;
   113:         weth = weth_;
